monsters.name: Bygone Effigy
monsters.pattern: starts with Sleep; Sleep -> Wake; Wake -> Slashes; Sleep Move -> Slashes; Slashes -> Slashes

pattern: The Bygone Effigy starts asleep and follows this sequence:
Sleep — does nothing on its first turn.
Wake — wakes up and gains 10 Strength.
notes: Bygone Effigy's Sleep phase does not feature an actual Debuff status, unlike Lagavulin Matriarch's Asleep or Slumbering Beetle's Slumber.
Because it gains 10 Strength before it begins attacking, the Bygone Effigy's attack always deals 23 ([A9: 25]) damage, although the attack itself technically deals only 13 ([A9: 15]).
Slow only increases damage from Attack cards, which means cards that apply effects to deal damage such as Poison, Doom, or Power effects like Serpent Form are unaffected.
When calculating damage for Slow, rounding always reduces damage down to the nearest whole number. For example, a Strike (base 6 damage) will deal:
6 damage at 0–1 Slow
7 damage at 2–3 Slow
8 damage at 4 Slow
9 damage at 5–6 Slow
10 damage at 7–8 Slow
11 damage at 9 Slow
12 damage at 10 Slow.
In the case of Multiplayer, each card played by any player will increase Slow for all players for the turn.

monsters.name: Ceremonial Beast
monsters.pattern: starts with Stamp; Stamp -> Plow; Plow -> Plow; Stun -> Beast Cry; Beast Cry -> Stomp; Stomp -> Crush; Crush -> Beast Cry

pattern: The Ceremonial Beast has two distinct phases.
Uses Stamp on the first turn, gaining Plow.
When its HP drops to the Plow threshold (150, or [A9: 160]), it immediately becomes Stunned and loses all Strength.
Phase 2: After being stunned, repeats this three-move cycle:
notes: Plow acts as a HP threshold: when the Ceremonial Beast's HP drops to the Plow amount or below, it is Stunned and loses all accumulated Strength. This effectively gives the player a free turn.

If the Ceremonial Beast's HP is already below the Plow threshold on the first turn (before it gains Plow), it will not become Stunned when it gains Plow. Instead, it acts normally until it loses any amount of HP, which will trigger the Plow effect like normal.
Ringing from Beast Cry limits the player to playing only 1 card on that turn.

During Phase 1, each Plow gains 2 Strength, but all of it is lost when the Ceremonial Beast's HP drops to the threshold. In Phase 2, each Crush gains 3 ([A9: 4]) Strength that accumulates for the rest of the battle.

monsters.pattern: starts with Bite; Respawn -> <conditional branch REVIVE_BRANCH>; Bite -> Skull Bash; Skull Bash -> Bite; Multi-Claw -> Multi-Claw; Lacerate -> Big Pounce; Big Pounce -> Burning Growl; Burning Growl -> Lacerate; conditional branch REVIVE_BRANCH: Multi-Claw if Respawns < 2 | Lacerate if Respawns >= 2

notes: Each of Test Subject's phases will lose all status effects when transitioning to the next phase, including the Strength gained from Enrage in the first phase.
Cards with on-kill or Fatal triggers (Feed, The Hunt, Knockout Blow, Sunder, and Hand of Greed) will trigger successfully during any of the Test Subject's phases.

Because the Test Subject is a Boss in Act 3, after which there are no opportunities to spend Gold or earn card rewards, Feed, Knockout Blow, and Sunder are the only cards with an on-kill or Fatal trigger that matters.
After Test Subject loses all its HP in a phase, it cannot be targeted by any cards until it revives into the next phase.

Cards with no targets can still be played, including Attack cards that hit all enemies or random enemies (such as Sword Boomerang or Sweeping Beam), but they will deal no damage. All other possible effects will still occur (for instance, Sweeping Beam will still draw a card).

monsters.pattern: starts with Pressurize; Pressurize -> Stomp; Stomp -> Ram; Ram -> Siphon; Siphon -> Pressure Gun; Pressure Gun -> Pressure Up; Pressure Up -> Stomp; About to Blow -> Explode; Explode -> Explode

pattern: The Waterfall Giant uses Pressurize on its first turn, then follows a repeating cycle:

Almost every move also adds 3 Steam Eruption. When the Waterfall Giant is killed while it has Steam Eruption, it becomes invulnerable and uses About To Blow, cleansing all its buffs and debuffs. Next turn it will use Explode, dealing damage equal to its accumulated Steam Eruption before dying.
If the Waterfall Giant is killed when it has no Steam Eruption (e.g. via Doom), it dies normally without triggering the explosion sequence.
notes: Even though the HP bar in the last phase shows as "infinity", it is actually set to the finite number of 999,999,999 HP. As such, it is theoretically possible to kill the Waterfall Giant in its last phase.
If a card both deals damage and applies a debuff like Neutralize, the damage can kill the Waterfall Giant and activate About To Blow, then the debuff will be applied.
